tinyweb used from C, with no Pyking: the library, how to build and run a program, and every function.

tinyweb's C implementation is a library of its own: a C program can use it to draw on a web page, add buttons, labels and sliders to it, play sounds and answer the reader, with no Pyking anywhere. It is the file Pyking copies beside a program compiled for `c23`, renamed `tinyweb.c`, `tinyweb.h`.

**Download** [tinyweb-c.zip](../../../tinyweb/c/tinyweb-c.zip): `tinyweb.c`, `tinyweb.h`, the example below, and the samples in `tinyweb_assets/`.

## Running a program

The program serves its own page: `web_init` starts the server and prints its address, and once the program's own code has finished it goes on serving the page and calling the functions it handed over until it is stopped (Ctrl-C). Open the address in a browser.

```sh
cc -o example example.c tinyweb.c
./example
```

The page asks for a sample beside where the program runs first, then in `tinyweb_assets/` there.

## An example

```c
/* A canvas, two circles, two samples and buttons that play them, written
   in C against tinyweb.c. Build it with
     cc -o example example.c tinyweb.c
   then run ./example and open the address it prints. */

#include <stdio.h>

#include "tinyweb.h"

static const char *kick;
static const char *snare;
static int presses = 0;

static void play_kick(void)
{
    tinyweb_command("play", kick, "", "0.0 1.0 1.0 0.0 0 0", 2);
}

static void play_snare(void)
{
    presses += 1;
    printf("snare, press %d\n", presses);
    tinyweb_command("play", snare, "", "0.0 0.5 1.0 0.0 0 0", 2);
}

static void nothing(void)
{
}

int main(void)
{
    const char *canvas;
    tinyweb_web_init(0);
    kick = tinyweb_load_sample("kick1.wav");
    snare = tinyweb_load_sample("snare1.wav");
    canvas = tinyweb_canvas(400, 200);
    tinyweb_draw_shape(canvas, "circle", "100 50 30", "#ff0000", "", 1.0, 1.0);
    tinyweb_draw_shape(canvas, "circle", "100 50 20", "#000000", "", 1.0, 1.0);
    tinyweb_make_button("Play kick", play_kick);
    tinyweb_make_button("Play snare", play_snare);
    tinyweb_make_button("Does nothing", nothing);
    tinyweb_splash();
    printf("built the page\n");
    return 0;
}
```

## Functions

Every function but `web_init` needs `web_init` to have been called first, or `PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG` to be set (below); otherwise it says so and the program ends with status 1.

### `web_init`

```c
void tinyweb_web_init(int port);
```

Serves the program's page on `port` and prints its address, `tinyweb: http://127.0.0.1:N/`; port 0 picks any free port. Call it before anything else. With `PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG` set it does nothing.

### `canvas`

```c
const char *tinyweb_canvas(int width, int height);
```

A new canvas, `width` by `height` pixels, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it: "canvas", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `fill_canvas`

```c
void tinyweb_fill_canvas(const char *c, const char *color);
```

Fills the whole canvas `c` with `color`, a CSS color such as `"#ff0000"` or `"red"`.

### `draw_shape`

```c
void tinyweb_draw_shape(const char *c, const char *kind, const char *numbers, const char *color, const char *outline, double width, double alpha);
```

One shape on the canvas `c`. `kind` is "rect", "circle", "ellipse", "arc", "line", "lines", "curve", "bezier", "polygon", "path" or "erase", and `numbers` its numbers as words: x y width height radius for a rect, x y r for a circle, x y rx ry for an ellipse, x y r start end (radians) for an arc, x1 y1 x2 y2 for a line, x1 y1 x2 y2 for each of many lines, x1 y1 cx cy x2 y2 for a curve, x1 y1 ax ay bx by x2 y2 for a bezier, x y x y ... for a polygon or a path, and x y width height for the rectangle `erase` makes transparent. It is filled with `color` and outlined with `outline`, `width` pixels thick, each unless it is "", at `alpha` from 0.0 to 1.0. A color may be a gradient: "linear-gradient(x1 y1 x2 y2); 0.0 red; 1.0 blue", "radial-gradient(x1 y1 r1 x2 y2 r2); ..." or "conic-gradient(x y angle); ...", each stop its place from 0.0 to 1.0 and a CSS color.

### `draw_text`

```c
void tinyweb_draw_text(const char *c, double x, double y, const char *words, const char *color, int size, const char *font, const char *align, const char *baseline, bool bold, const char *outline, double outline_width, double alpha);
```

`words` written on the canvas `c` at (`x`, `y`): its left end there, or with `align` "center" or "right" its middle or right end, and its top there, or with `baseline` "middle", "alphabetic" or "bottom" that part of it. `size` pixels high, in `font` ("" for the page's own), bold where `bold` is true, filled with `color` and outlined with `outline` `outline_width` pixels thick, each unless it is "", at `alpha`.

### `set_state`

```c
void tinyweb_set_state(const char *c, const char *kind, const char *value, const char *numbers);
```

Changes what the next drawing on the canvas `c` is drawn with. `kind` "translate", "rotate" or "scale" take their numbers (x y, radians, sx sy) in `numbers`; "push" and "pop" save and restore the state; "reset" takes every transformation off; "shadow" takes a color in `value` ("" for none) and blur dx dy in `numbers`; "blend" takes "normal" or "add" in `value`; "line_style" takes how lines end and turn in `value` ("round round", "butt miter", ...) and the dash offset followed by the dash and gap lengths in `numbers`; "clip" keeps what is drawn after it inside a shape, its kind in `value` and its numbers as `draw_shape` takes them. `fill_canvas` starts the canvas afresh.

### `measure`

```c
void tinyweb_measure(const char *words, int size, const char *font, bool bold, void (*answer)(double));
```

Asks the page how wide `words` is written `size` pixels high in `font`, bold where `bold` is true, and calls `answer` with the width in pixels once the page has said.

### `watch_pointer`

```c
void tinyweb_watch_pointer(const char *c, const char *kind, void (*f)(int, int));
```

Calls `f` with where the pointer is on the canvas `c`, in pixels from its top left corner, each time it goes down there (`kind` "press"), comes up ("release"), moves over it ("move") or moves with the button held ("drag").

### `pointer`

```c
int tinyweb_pointer(const char *c, const char *which);
```

Where the pointer was last seen on the canvas `c`: `which` "x" or "y" for its position, "down" for 1 while its button is held and 0 otherwise. The canvas reports the pointer once `watch_pointer` has been called for it.

### `draw_image`

```c
void tinyweb_draw_image(const char *c, const char *picture, int x, int y, int width, int height, double alpha);
```

Draws a loaded picture on the canvas `c`, its top left corner at (`x`, `y`), stretched to `width` by `height`, at `alpha`. One still loading is drawn once it has loaded, and what is drawn after it waits until then.

### `make_bitmap`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_bitmap(int width, int height, int background);
```

A picture `width` by `height` pixels the program builds, every pixel `background` to start with, as `set_pixel` takes a color, kept by the program: setting a pixel sends nothing. Answers the string that names it: "bitmap", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `set_pixel`

```c
void tinyweb_set_pixel(const char *b, int x, int y, int color);
```

Sets the pixel (`x`, `y`) of the bitmap `b` to `color`, red times 65536 plus green times 256 plus blue. A pixel outside it is left alone.

### `get_pixel`

```c
int tinyweb_get_pixel(const char *b, int x, int y);
```

The color of the pixel (`x`, `y`) of the bitmap `b`, as `set_pixel` takes one; 0 outside it.

### `fill_bitmap`

```c
void tinyweb_fill_bitmap(const char *b, int color);
```

Sets every pixel of the bitmap `b` to `color`.

### `draw_bitmap`

```c
void tinyweb_draw_bitmap(const char *c, const char *b, int x, int y, double scale);
```

Draws the bitmap `b` on the canvas `c`, its top left corner at (`x`, `y`), each pixel `scale` pixels across: sharp squares above 1.0. What changed since it was last drawn is sent to the page.

### `load_image`

```c
const char *tinyweb_load_image(const char *name);
```

Starts loading the picture `name`, looked for as a sample is, and answers the string that names it to `draw_image`.

### `make_button`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_button(const char *title, void (*on_click)(void));
```

A button showing `title`, placed below what the page already shows, which calls `on_click` each time it is pressed. Answers the string that names it: `title`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `label`

```c
const char *tinyweb_label(const char *text);
```

A line of text, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it to `set_label`: `text`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `row`

```c
const char *tinyweb_row(void);
```

A box placed below what the page already shows, whose elements go side by side, wrapping where the page is too narrow. Answers the string that names it to `inside`: "row", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `column`

```c
const char *tinyweb_column(void);
```

A box whose elements go one below another, as the page's own do: inside a row, it stands beside the row's other elements. Answers the string that names it to `inside`.

### `inside`

```c
void tinyweb_inside(const char *id);
```

Makes every element made after it go into the row or column `id`, until `outside` or another `inside`.

### `outside`

```c
void tinyweb_outside(void);
```

Makes every element made after it go on the page again, below what is there.

### `set_label`

```c
void tinyweb_set_label(const char *id, const char *text);
```

Replaces the text of the label `id`, or the title of the button `id`, with `text`.

### `make_slider`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_slider(int low, int high, int value, void (*on_change)(int));
```

A slider from `low` to `high`, starting at `value`, placed below what the page already shows, which calls `on_change` with each new value it is moved to. Answers the string that names it: "slider", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `make_checkbox`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_checkbox(const char *title, bool checked, void (*on_change)(bool));
```

A checkbox showing `title`, ticked where `checked` is true, which calls `on_change` with whether it is ticked each time the reader changes it. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_radio`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_radio(const char *group, const char *title, bool chosen, void (*on_pick)(const char *));
```

A radio button showing `title` in the group `group`: choosing one clears the others. The first of a group starts chosen unless one says `chosen`. Calls `on_pick` with `title` when the reader chooses it. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_choice`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_choice(const char *options, int chosen, void (*on_change)(int));
```

A dropdown of `options`, one per line, the one at position `chosen` chosen, which calls `on_change` with the position the reader chooses. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_text_input`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_text_input(const char *placeholder, void (*on_enter)(const char *));
```

A line to type text into, showing `placeholder` while empty, which calls `on_enter` with the text when Enter is pressed in it. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_number_input`

```c
const char *tinyweb_make_number_input(int low, int high, int value, void (*on_change)(int));
```

A field for a whole number from `low` to `high`, starting at `value`, which calls `on_change` with each new number. Answers the string that names it.

### `set_checked`

```c
void tinyweb_set_checked(const char *id, bool checked);
```

Ticks or clears the checkbox `id`, or chooses the radio button `id`.

### `set_value`

```c
void tinyweb_set_value(const char *id, int value);
```

Moves the slider or number field `id` to `value`, or picks the dropdown choice at that position.

### `apply_style`

```c
void tinyweb_apply_style(const char *id, const char *kind, const char *property, const char *value);
```

Changes the page's look. With `kind` "theme", `value` names a theme: "light" (the default), "dark", "plain", "paper" or "retro". With `kind` "page", "button", "label", "slider" or "canvas", `property` of every element of that kind becomes `value`; with `kind` "element", only the element `id`'s. `property` is one of background, color, border, radius, font, size, padding, gap, accent and width, and `value` is CSS, such as "#336699" or "12px". `id` is "" except for an element.

### `load_sample`

```c
const char *tinyweb_load_sample(const char *name);
```

Starts loading the sound file `name` and answers a string naming it to `play_sample`: `name`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. The name is looked up beside where the program runs first, and then among the samples tinyweb ships in `tinyweb_assets/`: kick1.wav, snare1.wav, hihat1.wav and piano_c1.wav.

### `fresh_id`

```c
const char *tinyweb_fresh_id(const char *name);
```

A new element's identifier: `name`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. Sends nothing; what `command` makes takes it.

### `command`

```c
void tinyweb_command(const char *kind, const char *id, const char *text, const char *numbers, int mode);
```

Sends the page one command, by `kind`, with an element `id`, a `text` and its `numbers` as words. Sound: "play" (id the sample; numbers at volume rate pan channel reverse), "start" (id a new voice, text the sample, numbers as play's then loop), "stop" (at), "fade" (volume over), "stop_all", "tone" (text the wave; frequency at duration volume pan channel), "master" (volume), "tempo" (bpm), "swing" (amount), "beat" (steps; reports "beat" for `id`), "channel" (id the channel; volume pan echo echo_time feedback reverb low_pass), "listen" (bins smoothing), "audio" (text pause or resume), "render" and "render_end". Timers: "after" and "every" (seconds; reports "timer"), "cancel". The page: "set_text", "visible" and "enabled" (1 or 0), "remove", "text_area" (rows columns), "file_button", "cursor", "save_canvas", "download". `mode` says what a page connecting later is sent again: 0 kept, 1 the last of its kind and id, 2 like a sound, 3 nothing.

### `watch`

```c
void tinyweb_watch(const char *id, const char *kind, void (*f)(void));
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`: a timer's "timer", a beat's "beat", a text area's "change", a file button's "loaded", a rendering's "rendered".

### `report_number`

```c
double tinyweb_report_number(const char *name, int k);
```

The `k`th number the page last reported under `name`: "clock" (the beat, the latency, whether sound runs), "beat" (a beat's step and time), "level", "band" and "wave" once listening, "rendered" (seconds taken, peak). 0.0 where there is none.

### `report_text`

```c
const char *tinyweb_report_text(const char *name);
```

The text the page last reported under `name`: "value." and an input's identifier for what it holds, "file" and "file.text" for a file loaded. Empty where there is none.

### `report_count`

```c
int tinyweb_report_count(const char *name);
```

How many numbers the page last reported under `name`.

### `watch_text`

```c
void tinyweb_watch_text(const char *id, const char *kind, const char *name, void (*f)(const char *));
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`, with the text it last reported under `name`: a text area's "change" with "value." and its identifier, a file button's "loaded" with "file".

### `watch_step`

```c
void tinyweb_watch_step(const char *id, const char *kind, void (*f)(int, double));
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`, with the first number reported under `kind` as a whole number and the second: a beat's step and when it sounds.

### `watch_pair`

```c
void tinyweb_watch_pair(const char *id, const char *kind, void (*f)(double, double));
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`, with the first two numbers reported under `kind`: a rendering's seconds taken and its peak.

### `splash`

```c
void tinyweb_splash(void);
```

Shows the splash screen: the page dimmed, and a message asking the reader to click, since a browser plays no sound before the reader has clicked or pressed a key. The page waits there -- what the program draws next, its frames and its clock -- until the reader does. It is shown at most once, and not at all where the reader has already clicked. The first `play_sample` before a click shows it too; a program that plays sound only from callbacks calls it at the end of its main code.

### `set_splash`

```c
void tinyweb_set_splash(const char *message);
```

Sets what the splash screen says, "Click to Start" until it is set. An empty `message` turns the splash screen off.

### `time`

```c
double tinyweb_time(void);
```

The page's clock, in seconds, as the page last reported it: inside an `on_frame` callback, the time the frame is for. It is the audio clock once sound has started, so a time read here is a time `play_sample` can be given.

### `sdelay`

```c
void tinyweb_sdelay(double time);
```

Waits until the page's audio clock is `time` seconds after the last `sdelay` ended (after now, for the first), so a loop of them does not drift; one that has fallen behind goes on at once. The page's events are delivered while it waits, and a sound played next with no time of its own starts exactly at the end.

### `on_frame`

```c
void tinyweb_on_frame(void (*draw)(double));
```

Calls `draw` before each frame the page shows, with the time the frame is for.

### `on_mouse`

```c
void tinyweb_on_mouse(const char *c, void (*click)(int, int));
```

Calls `click` with the position, in pixels from the top left corner, of every click on the canvas `c`.

### `on_key`

```c
void tinyweb_on_key(void (*pressed)(const char *));
```

Calls `pressed` with the name of every key pressed while the page has the focus: a letter or digit as itself, and otherwise the browser's name for it, such as "ArrowLeft", "Enter" or " ".

### `on_key_up`

```c
void tinyweb_on_key_up(void (*released)(const char *));
```

Calls `released` with the name of each key let go while the page has the focus. Leaving the page lets go of every key held.

### `key_down`

```c
bool tinyweb_key_down(const char *key);
```

Whether the key named `key` is held down now.

## Without a page

Two environment variables, each a file path, run a program with no page at all, which is how it is tested: with `PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG` set, every command the program would send its page is appended to that file as one line, and once the program's own code has finished the events `PYKING_TINYWEB_EVENTS` lists -- `click ID`, `slide ID VALUE`, `check ID true`, `pick ID`, `choose ID INDEX`, `enter ID TEXT`, `frame T`, `mouse ID X Y`, `press ID X Y`, `move ID X Y`, `release ID X Y`, `key NAME`, `key_up NAME` and `measured ID WIDTH`, one per line, each ID and TEXT a quoted string -- are delivered as if a reader had caused them.

```sh
PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG=page.log PYKING_TINYWEB_EVENTS=clicks.txt ./example
```

## What Pyking generates

Pyking's own tinyweb tests, compiled for `c23`. Each comes with the libraries it needs as Pyking writes them -- tinyweb's implementation under its own name, and the module Pyking compiles from tinyweb's Pyking half -- and is built and run with:

```sh
cc -std=c23 -o program tinyweb_external.c tinyweb.c program.c
./program
```

# tinyweb's bitmaps: pixels set, read back and filled, shown at several
# scales, with only what changed since the last showing sent each time.
import tinyweb as tw

tw.web_init(0)

    string(p.r) + " " + string(p.g) + " " + string(p.b)


b = bitmap.bitmap(16, 10)
print("a new bitmap is white:", show(bitmap.get_pixel(b, 3, 3)))
print("or its background:", show(bitmap.get_pixel(bitmap.bitmap(2, 2, color.green), 1, 1)))
for y in range(10):
    for x in range(16):
        bitmap.set_pixel(b, x, y, color.rgb(x * 16, y * 25, 128))
bitmap.show_bitmap(c, b, scale = 10.0)
orange = color.rgb(255, 136, 0)
bitmap.set_pixel(b, 4, 2, orange)
bitmap.set_pixel(b, 7, 5, orange)
bitmap.set_pixel(b, 40, 2, orange)
print("pixel (4, 2):", show(bitmap.get_pixel(b, 4, 2)), "outside:", show(bitmap.get_pixel(b, -1, 0)), bitmap.get_pixel(b, -1, 0).a)
bitmap.show_bitmap(c, b, 0, 0, 10.0)
bitmap.show_bitmap(c, b, 5, 5)
small = bitmap.bitmap(4, 4)
bitmap.fill_bitmap(small, color.blue)
print("filled:", bitmap.get_pixel(small, 3, 3).b)


def frame(t: Float):
    bitmap.set_pixel(small, 1, 1, color.rgb(int(t * 100.0), 0, 0))
    bitmap.show_bitmap(c, small, 120, 60, 2.0)


bitmap.show_bitmap(c, small, 120, 60, 0.5)
tw.on_frame(frame)

# The mouse, the keyboard and a slider, each reported on a label, and
# the other drawing functions. The .events file clicks the canvas,
# presses two keys -- the second Enter -- and moves the slider.

import tinyweb as tw
import tinyweb.color as color

tw.web_init(0)

c = tw.canvas(300, 200)
tw.rect(c, 0, 0, 300, 200, color.hex(0xeeeeee))
tw.line(c, 0, 0, 300, 200)
tw.line(c, 0, 200, 300, 0, color.red, width = 3)
tw.text(c, 10, 10, "click \"me\"", size = 20)
status = tw.label("nothing yet")

def clicked(x: Int, y: Int):
    tw.set_text(status, "clicked at " + string(x) + ", " + string(y))
    tw.circle(c, x, y, 5, color.blue)

def pressed(key: String):
    print("key [" + key + "]")
    if key == "Enter":
        tw.play_file("snare1.wav")

def moved(value: Int):
    tw.set_text(status, "slider at " + string(value))

tw.on_click(c, clicked)
tw.on_key(pressed)
tw.slider(0, 10, 5, on_change = moved)
tw.slider(1, 3, 2)

    print("press at", x, y, "down", tw.mouse(c).down)
    tw.circle(c, x, y, 4, color.hex(0xdc143c))


def dragged(x: Int, y: Int):
    print("drag to", x, y, "down", tw.mouse(c).down)
    tw.line(c, 0, 0, x, y, color.black, 2)


def moved(x: Int, y: Int):
    print("move to", x, y, "down", tw.mouse(c).down)


def released(x: Int, y: Int):
    print("release at", x, y, "down", tw.mouse(c).down)


def nothing(x: Int, y: Int):

tw.on_drag(c, dragged)
tw.on_move(c, moved)
tw.on_release(c, released)
tw.on_move(other, nothing)
start = tw.mouse(c)
print("before any event", start.x, start.y, start.down)


def let_go(key: String):
    print("let go of", key, "still held:", tw.key_down(key))


tw.on_key_up(let_go)


def frame(t: Float):
    left = tw.key_down("ArrowLeft")
    right = tw.key_down("ArrowRight")
    print("frame", t, "left", left, "right", right)


tw.on_frame(frame)

# tinyweb's `sdelay` in a loop that does not end by itself: each round
# plays a note, prints, draws and waits, a quarter of a second after the
# last wait ended rather than after the call. The eighth round leaves

var round = 0
loop:
    tw.play(piano)
    print("round", round, "at", tw.time())
    tw.circle(c, 10 + 20 * round, 20, 8, color.orange)
    round := round + 1
    if round == 8:
        break
    tw.sdelay(if round == 4 then 0.5 else 0.25)

tw.push(c)

tw.pop(c)

tw.pop(c)

    if (x < -DBL_MAX) { strcpy(out, "-inf"); return out; }
    negative = x < 0.0 || (x == 0.0 && 1.0 / x < 0.0);
    a = negative ? -x : x;
    if (a == 0.0) { strcpy(out, negative ? "-0.0" : "0.0"); return out; }
    for (p = 0; p < 16; p++) {
        sprintf(buf, "%.*e", p, a);
        if (strtod(buf, NULL) == a) break;
    }
    if (p == 16) sprintf(buf, "%.*e", 16, a);
    e = strchr(buf, 'e');
    at = (int)(e - buf);
    n = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < at; i++) if (buf[i] != '.') digits[n++] = buf[i];
    while (n > 1 && digits[n - 1] == '0') n--;
    digits[n] = '\0';
    decpt = atoi(e + 1) + 1;
    k = 0;
    if (negative) out[k++] = '-';
    if (decpt <= -4 || decpt > 16) {
        out[k++] = digits[0];
        if (n > 1) { out[k++] = '.'; strcpy(out + k, digits + 1); k += n - 1; }
        sprintf(out + k, "e%d", decpt - 1);
        return out;
    }
    if (decpt <= 0) {
        out[k++] = '0';
        out[k++] = '.';
        for (i = 0; i < -decpt; i++) out[k++] = '0';
        strcpy(out + k, digits);
        return out;
    }
    if (decpt >= n) {
        strcpy(out + k, digits);
        k += n;
        for (i = 0; i < decpt - n; i++) out[k++] = '0';
        strcpy(out + k, ".0");
        return out;
    }
    for (i = 0; i < decpt; i++) out[k++] = digits[i];
    out[k++] = '.';
    strcpy(out + k, digits + decpt);
    return out;
}

def tick():

def once():

tinyweb’s C implementation is a library of its own: a C program can use it to draw on a web page, add buttons, labels and sliders to it, play sounds and answer the reader, with no Pyking anywhere. It is the file Pyking copies beside a program compiled for c23, renamed tinyweb.c, tinyweb.h.

Download tinyweb-c.zip: tinyweb.c, tinyweb.h, the example below, and the samples in tinyweb_assets/.

Running a program

The program serves its own page: web_init starts the server and prints its address, and once the program’s own code has finished it goes on serving the page and calling the functions it handed over until it is stopped (Ctrl-C). Open the address in a browser.

The page asks for a sample beside where the program runs first, then in tinyweb_assets/ there.

An example

Functions

Every function but web_init needs web_init to have been called first, or PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG to be set (below); otherwise it says so and the program ends with status 1.

web_init

Serves the program’s page on port and prints its address, tinyweb: http://127.0.0.1:N/; port 0 picks any free port. Call it before anything else. With PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG set it does nothing.

canvas

A new canvas, width by height pixels, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it: “canvas”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

fill_canvas

Fills the whole canvas c with color, a CSS color such as "#ff0000" or "red".

draw_shape

One shape on the canvas c. kind is “rect”, “circle”, “ellipse”, “arc”, “line”, “lines”, “curve”, “bezier”, “polygon”, “path” or “erase”, and numbers its numbers as words: x y width height radius for a rect, x y r for a circle, x y rx ry for an ellipse, x y r start end (radians) for an arc, x1 y1 x2 y2 for a line, x1 y1 x2 y2 for each of many lines, x1 y1 cx cy x2 y2 for a curve, x1 y1 ax ay bx by x2 y2 for a bezier, x y x y … for a polygon or a path, and x y width height for the rectangle erase makes transparent. It is filled with color and outlined with outline, width pixels thick, each unless it is "", at alpha from 0.0 to 1.0. A color may be a gradient: “linear-gradient(x1 y1 x2 y2); 0.0 red; 1.0 blue”, “radial-gradient(x1 y1 r1 x2 y2 r2); …” or “conic-gradient(x y angle); …”, each stop its place from 0.0 to 1.0 and a CSS color.

draw_text

words written on the canvas c at (x, y): its left end there, or with align “center” or “right” its middle or right end, and its top there, or with baseline “middle”, “alphabetic” or “bottom” that part of it. size pixels high, in font ("" for the page’s own), bold where bold is true, filled with color and outlined with outline outline_width pixels thick, each unless it is "", at alpha.

set_state

Changes what the next drawing on the canvas c is drawn with. kind “translate”, “rotate” or “scale” take their numbers (x y, radians, sx sy) in numbers; “push” and “pop” save and restore the state; “reset” takes every transformation off; “shadow” takes a color in value ("" for none) and blur dx dy in numbers; “blend” takes “normal” or “add” in value; “line_style” takes how lines end and turn in value (“round round”, “butt miter”, …) and the dash offset followed by the dash and gap lengths in numbers; “clip” keeps what is drawn after it inside a shape, its kind in value and its numbers as draw_shape takes them. fill_canvas starts the canvas afresh.

measure

Asks the page how wide words is written size pixels high in font, bold where bold is true, and calls answer with the width in pixels once the page has said.

watch_pointer

Calls f with where the pointer is on the canvas c, in pixels from its top left corner, each time it goes down there (kind “press”), comes up (“release”), moves over it (“move”) or moves with the button held (“drag”).

pointer

Where the pointer was last seen on the canvas c: which “x” or “y” for its position, “down” for 1 while its button is held and 0 otherwise. The canvas reports the pointer once watch_pointer has been called for it.

draw_image

Draws a loaded picture on the canvas c, its top left corner at (x, y), stretched to width by height, at alpha. One still loading is drawn once it has loaded, and what is drawn after it waits until then.

make_bitmap

A picture width by height pixels the program builds, every pixel background to start with, as set_pixel takes a color, kept by the program: setting a pixel sends nothing. Answers the string that names it: “bitmap”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

set_pixel

Sets the pixel (x, y) of the bitmap b to color, red times 65536 plus green times 256 plus blue. A pixel outside it is left alone.

get_pixel

The color of the pixel (x, y) of the bitmap b, as set_pixel takes one; 0 outside it.

fill_bitmap

Sets every pixel of the bitmap b to color.

draw_bitmap

Draws the bitmap b on the canvas c, its top left corner at (x, y), each pixel scale pixels across: sharp squares above 1.0. What changed since it was last drawn is sent to the page.

load_image

Starts loading the picture name, looked for as a sample is, and answers the string that names it to draw_image.

make_button

A button showing title, placed below what the page already shows, which calls on_click each time it is pressed. Answers the string that names it: title, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

label

A line of text, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it to set_label: text, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

row

A box placed below what the page already shows, whose elements go side by side, wrapping where the page is too narrow. Answers the string that names it to inside: “row”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

column

A box whose elements go one below another, as the page’s own do: inside a row, it stands beside the row’s other elements. Answers the string that names it to inside.

inside

Makes every element made after it go into the row or column id, until outside or another inside.

outside

Makes every element made after it go on the page again, below what is there.

set_label

Replaces the text of the label id, or the title of the button id, with text.

make_slider

A slider from low to high, starting at value, placed below what the page already shows, which calls on_change with each new value it is moved to. Answers the string that names it: “slider”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

make_checkbox

A checkbox showing title, ticked where checked is true, which calls on_change with whether it is ticked each time the reader changes it. Answers the string that names it.

make_radio

A radio button showing title in the group group: choosing one clears the others. The first of a group starts chosen unless one says chosen. Calls on_pick with title when the reader chooses it. Answers the string that names it.

make_choice

A dropdown of options, one per line, the one at position chosen chosen, which calls on_change with the position the reader chooses. Answers the string that names it.

make_text_input

A line to type text into, showing placeholder while empty, which calls on_enter with the text when Enter is pressed in it. Answers the string that names it.

make_number_input

A field for a whole number from low to high, starting at value, which calls on_change with each new number. Answers the string that names it.

set_checked

Ticks or clears the checkbox id, or chooses the radio button id.

set_value

Moves the slider or number field id to value, or picks the dropdown choice at that position.

apply_style

Changes the page’s look. With kind “theme”, value names a theme: “light” (the default), “dark”, “plain”, “paper” or “retro”. With kind “page”, “button”, “label”, “slider” or “canvas”, property of every element of that kind becomes value; with kind “element”, only the element id’s. property is one of background, color, border, radius, font, size, padding, gap, accent and width, and value is CSS, such as “#336699” or “12px”. id is "" except for an element.

load_sample

Starts loading the sound file name and answers a string naming it to play_sample: name, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. The name is looked up beside where the program runs first, and then among the samples tinyweb ships in tinyweb_assets/: kick1.wav, snare1.wav, hihat1.wav and piano_c1.wav.

fresh_id

A new element’s identifier: name, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. Sends nothing; what command makes takes it.

command

Sends the page one command, by kind, with an element id, a text and its numbers as words. Sound: “play” (id the sample; numbers at volume rate pan channel reverse), “start” (id a new voice, text the sample, numbers as play’s then loop), “stop” (at), “fade” (volume over), “stop_all”, “tone” (text the wave; frequency at duration volume pan channel), “master” (volume), “tempo” (bpm), “swing” (amount), “beat” (steps; reports “beat” for id), “channel” (id the channel; volume pan echo echo_time feedback reverb low_pass), “listen” (bins smoothing), “audio” (text pause or resume), “render” and “render_end”. Timers: “after” and “every” (seconds; reports “timer”), “cancel”. The page: “set_text”, “visible” and “enabled” (1 or 0), “remove”, “text_area” (rows columns), “file_button”, “cursor”, “save_canvas”, “download”. mode says what a page connecting later is sent again: 0 kept, 1 the last of its kind and id, 2 like a sound, 3 nothing.

watch

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id: a timer’s “timer”, a beat’s “beat”, a text area’s “change”, a file button’s “loaded”, a rendering’s “rendered”.

report_number

The kth number the page last reported under name: “clock” (the beat, the latency, whether sound runs), “beat” (a beat’s step and time), “level”, “band” and “wave” once listening, “rendered” (seconds taken, peak). 0.0 where there is none.

report_text

The text the page last reported under name: “value.” and an input’s identifier for what it holds, “file” and “file.text” for a file loaded. Empty where there is none.

report_count

How many numbers the page last reported under name.

watch_text

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id, with the text it last reported under name: a text area’s “change” with “value.” and its identifier, a file button’s “loaded” with “file”.

watch_step

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id, with the first number reported under kind as a whole number and the second: a beat’s step and when it sounds.

watch_pair

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id, with the first two numbers reported under kind: a rendering’s seconds taken and its peak.

splash

Shows the splash screen: the page dimmed, and a message asking the reader to click, since a browser plays no sound before the reader has clicked or pressed a key. The page waits there — what the program draws next, its frames and its clock — until the reader does. It is shown at most once, and not at all where the reader has already clicked. The first play_sample before a click shows it too; a program that plays sound only from callbacks calls it at the end of its main code.

set_splash

Sets what the splash screen says, “Click to Start” until it is set. An empty message turns the splash screen off.

time

The page’s clock, in seconds, as the page last reported it: inside an on_frame callback, the time the frame is for. It is the audio clock once sound has started, so a time read here is a time play_sample can be given.

sdelay

Waits until the page’s audio clock is time seconds after the last sdelay ended (after now, for the first), so a loop of them does not drift; one that has fallen behind goes on at once. The page’s events are delivered while it waits, and a sound played next with no time of its own starts exactly at the end.

on_frame

Calls draw before each frame the page shows, with the time the frame is for.

on_mouse

Calls click with the position, in pixels from the top left corner, of every click on the canvas c.

on_key

Calls pressed with the name of every key pressed while the page has the focus: a letter or digit as itself, and otherwise the browser’s name for it, such as “ArrowLeft”, “Enter” or ” ”.

on_key_up

Calls released with the name of each key let go while the page has the focus. Leaving the page lets go of every key held.

key_down

Whether the key named key is held down now.

Without a page

tinyweb used from Java, with no Pyking: the library, how to build and run a program, and every function.

tinyweb's Java implementation is a library of its own: a Java program can use it to draw on a web page, add buttons, labels and sliders to it, play sounds and answer the reader, with no Pyking anywhere. It is the file Pyking copies beside a program compiled for `java21`, renamed `Tinyweb.java`.

**Download** [tinyweb-java.zip](../../../tinyweb/java/tinyweb-java.zip): `Tinyweb.java`, the example below, and the samples in `tinyweb_assets/`.

## Running a program

The program serves its own page: `web_init` starts the server and prints its address, and once the program's own code has finished it goes on serving the page and calling the functions it handed over until it is stopped (Ctrl-C). Open the address in a browser.

```sh
javac Tinyweb.java Example.java
java Example
```

The page asks for a sample beside where the program runs first, then in `tinyweb_assets/` there.

## An example

```java
// A canvas, two circles, two samples and buttons that play them, written
// in Java against Tinyweb.java. Build it with
//   javac Tinyweb.java Example.java
// then run `java Example` and open the address it prints.

public final class Example {

    private static int presses = 0;

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Tinyweb.web_init(0);
        String kick = Tinyweb.load_sample("kick1.wav");
        String snare = Tinyweb.load_sample("snare1.wav");
        String canvas = Tinyweb.canvas(400, 200);
        Tinyweb.draw_shape(canvas, "circle", "100 50 30", "#ff0000", "", 1.0, 1.0);
        Tinyweb.draw_shape(canvas, "circle", "100 50 20", "#000000", "", 1.0, 1.0);
        Tinyweb.make_button("Play kick", () -> Tinyweb.command("play", kick, "", "0.0 1.0 1.0 0.0 0 0", 2));
        Tinyweb.make_button("Play snare", () -> {
            presses += 1;
            System.out.println("snare, press " + presses);
            Tinyweb.command("play", snare, "", "0.0 0.5 1.0 0.0 0 0", 2);
        });
        Tinyweb.make_button("Does nothing", () -> { });
        Tinyweb.splash();
        System.out.println("built the page");
    }
}
```

## Functions

Every function but `web_init` needs `web_init` to have been called first, or `PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG` to be set (below); otherwise it says so and the program ends with status 1.

### `web_init`

```java
public static void web_init(int port)
```

Serves the program's page on `port` and prints its address, `tinyweb: http://127.0.0.1:N/`; port 0 picks any free port. Call it before anything else. With `PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG` set it does nothing.

### `canvas`

```java
public static String canvas(int width, int height)
```

A new canvas, `width` by `height` pixels, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it: "canvas", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `fill_canvas`

```java
public static void fill_canvas(String c, String color)
```

Fills the whole canvas `c` with `color`, a CSS color such as `"#ff0000"` or `"red"`.

### `draw_shape`

```java
public static void draw_shape(String c, String kind, String numbers, String color, String outline, double width, double alpha)
```

One shape on the canvas `c`. `kind` is "rect", "circle", "ellipse", "arc", "line", "lines", "curve", "bezier", "polygon", "path" or "erase", and `numbers` its numbers as words: x y width height radius for a rect, x y r for a circle, x y rx ry for an ellipse, x y r start end (radians) for an arc, x1 y1 x2 y2 for a line, x1 y1 x2 y2 for each of many lines, x1 y1 cx cy x2 y2 for a curve, x1 y1 ax ay bx by x2 y2 for a bezier, x y x y ... for a polygon or a path, and x y width height for the rectangle `erase` makes transparent. It is filled with `color` and outlined with `outline`, `width` pixels thick, each unless it is "", at `alpha` from 0.0 to 1.0. A color may be a gradient: "linear-gradient(x1 y1 x2 y2); 0.0 red; 1.0 blue", "radial-gradient(x1 y1 r1 x2 y2 r2); ..." or "conic-gradient(x y angle); ...", each stop its place from 0.0 to 1.0 and a CSS color.

### `draw_pairs`

```java
public static void draw_pairs(String c, String kind, java.util.List<?> items, String color, String outline, double width, double alpha)
```

Many shapes' numbers in one go, as a list rather than as words: `kind` "polygon" or "path" through the points (x, y) in `items`, drawn as `draw_shape` draws one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

### `draw_triples`

```java
public static void draw_triples(String c, String kind, java.util.List<?> items, String color, String outline, double width, double alpha)
```

Many circles in one go: `kind` "circles", each (x, y, radius) in `items` filled and outlined on its own, as `draw_shape` draws one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

### `draw_quads`

```java
public static void draw_quads(String c, String kind, java.util.List<?> items, String color, String outline, double width, double alpha)
```

Many separate lines in one go: `kind` "lines", each (x1, y1, x2, y2) in `items`, stroked together as one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

### `draw_text`

```java
public static void draw_text(String c, double x, double y, String words, String color, int size, String font, String align, String baseline, boolean bold, String outline, double outline_width, double alpha)
```

`words` written on the canvas `c` at (`x`, `y`): its left end there, or with `align` "center" or "right" its middle or right end, and its top there, or with `baseline` "middle", "alphabetic" or "bottom" that part of it. `size` pixels high, in `font` ("" for the page's own), bold where `bold` is true, filled with `color` and outlined with `outline` `outline_width` pixels thick, each unless it is "", at `alpha`.

### `set_state`

```java
public static void set_state(String c, String kind, String value, String numbers)
```

Changes what the next drawing on the canvas `c` is drawn with. `kind` "translate", "rotate" or "scale" take their numbers (x y, radians, sx sy) in `numbers`; "push" and "pop" save and restore the state; "reset" takes every transformation off; "shadow" takes a color in `value` ("" for none) and blur dx dy in `numbers`; "blend" takes "normal" or "add" in `value`; "line_style" takes how lines end and turn in `value` ("round round", "butt miter", ...) and the dash offset followed by the dash and gap lengths in `numbers`; "clip" keeps what is drawn after it inside a shape, its kind in `value` and its numbers as `draw_shape` takes them. `fill_canvas` starts the canvas afresh.

### `measure`

```java
public static void measure(String words, int size, String font, boolean bold, Consumer<Double> answer)
```

Asks the page how wide `words` is written `size` pixels high in `font`, bold where `bold` is true, and calls `answer` with the width in pixels once the page has said.

### `watch_pointer`

```java
public static void watch_pointer(String c, String kind, BiConsumer<Integer, Integer> f)
```

Calls `f` with where the pointer is on the canvas `c`, in pixels from its top left corner, each time it goes down there (`kind` "press"), comes up ("release"), moves over it ("move") or moves with the button held ("drag").

### `pointer`

```java
public static int pointer(String c, String which)
```

Where the pointer was last seen on the canvas `c`: `which` "x" or "y" for its position, "down" for 1 while its button is held and 0 otherwise. The canvas reports the pointer once `watch_pointer` has been called for it.

### `draw_image`

```java
public static void draw_image(String c, String picture, int x, int y, int width, int height, double alpha)
```

Draws a loaded picture on the canvas `c`, its top left corner at (`x`, `y`), stretched to `width` by `height`, at `alpha`. One still loading is drawn once it has loaded, and what is drawn after it waits until then.

### `make_bitmap`

```java
public static String make_bitmap(int width, int height, int background)
```

A picture `width` by `height` pixels the program builds, every pixel `background` to start with, as `set_pixel` takes a color, kept by the program: setting a pixel sends nothing. Answers the string that names it: "bitmap", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `set_pixel`

```java
public static void set_pixel(String b, int x, int y, int color)
```

Sets the pixel (`x`, `y`) of the bitmap `b` to `color`, red times 65536 plus green times 256 plus blue. A pixel outside it is left alone.

### `get_pixel`

```java
public static int get_pixel(String b, int x, int y)
```

The color of the pixel (`x`, `y`) of the bitmap `b`, as `set_pixel` takes one; 0 outside it.

### `fill_bitmap`

```java
public static void fill_bitmap(String b, int color)
```

Sets every pixel of the bitmap `b` to `color`.

### `draw_bitmap`

```java
public static void draw_bitmap(String c, String b, int x, int y, double scale)
```

Draws the bitmap `b` on the canvas `c`, its top left corner at (`x`, `y`), each pixel `scale` pixels across: sharp squares above 1.0. What changed since it was last drawn is sent to the page.

### `load_image`

```java
public static String load_image(String name)
```

Starts loading the picture `name`, looked for as a sample is, and answers the string that names it to `draw_image`.

### `make_button`

```java
public static String make_button(String title, Runnable on_click)
```

A button showing `title`, placed below what the page already shows, which calls `on_click` each time it is pressed. Answers the string that names it: `title`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `label`

```java
public static String label(String text)
```

A line of text, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it to `set_label`: `text`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `row`

```java
public static String row()
```

A box placed below what the page already shows, whose elements go side by side, wrapping where the page is too narrow. Answers the string that names it to `inside`: "row", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `column`

```java
public static String column()
```

A box whose elements go one below another, as the page's own do: inside a row, it stands beside the row's other elements. Answers the string that names it to `inside`.

### `inside`

```java
public static void inside(String id)
```

Makes every element made after it go into the row or column `id`, until `outside` or another `inside`.

### `outside`

```java
public static void outside()
```

Makes every element made after it go on the page again, below what is there.

### `set_label`

```java
public static void set_label(String id, String text)
```

Replaces the text of the label `id`, or the title of the button `id`, with `text`.

### `make_slider`

```java
public static String make_slider(int low, int high, int value, Consumer<Integer> on_change)
```

A slider from `low` to `high`, starting at `value`, placed below what the page already shows, which calls `on_change` with each new value it is moved to. Answers the string that names it: "slider", with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

### `make_checkbox`

```java
public static String make_checkbox(String title, boolean checked, Consumer<Boolean> on_change)
```

A checkbox showing `title`, ticked where `checked` is true, which calls `on_change` with whether it is ticked each time the reader changes it. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_radio`

```java
public static String make_radio(String group, String title, boolean chosen, Consumer<String> on_pick)
```

A radio button showing `title` in the group `group`: choosing one clears the others. The first of a group starts chosen unless one says `chosen`. Calls `on_pick` with `title` when the reader chooses it. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_choice`

```java
public static String make_choice(String options, int chosen, Consumer<Integer> on_change)
```

A dropdown of `options`, one per line, the one at position `chosen` chosen, which calls `on_change` with the position the reader chooses. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_text_input`

```java
public static String make_text_input(String placeholder, Consumer<String> on_enter)
```

A line to type text into, showing `placeholder` while empty, which calls `on_enter` with the text when Enter is pressed in it. Answers the string that names it.

### `make_number_input`

```java
public static String make_number_input(int low, int high, int value, Consumer<Integer> on_change)
```

A field for a whole number from `low` to `high`, starting at `value`, which calls `on_change` with each new number. Answers the string that names it.

### `set_checked`

```java
public static void set_checked(String id, boolean checked)
```

Ticks or clears the checkbox `id`, or chooses the radio button `id`.

### `set_value`

```java
public static void set_value(String id, int value)
```

Moves the slider or number field `id` to `value`, or picks the dropdown choice at that position.

### `apply_style`

```java
public static void apply_style(String id, String kind, String property, String value)
```

Changes the page's look. With `kind` "theme", `value` names a theme: "light" (the default), "dark", "plain", "paper" or "retro". With `kind` "page", "button", "label", "slider" or "canvas", `property` of every element of that kind becomes `value`; with `kind` "element", only the element `id`'s. `property` is one of background, color, border, radius, font, size, padding, gap, accent and width, and `value` is CSS, such as "#336699" or "12px". `id` is "" except for an element.

### `load_sample`

```java
public static String load_sample(String name)
```

Starts loading the sound file `name` and answers a string naming it to `play_sample`: `name`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. The name is looked up beside where the program runs first, and then among the samples tinyweb ships in `tinyweb_assets/`: kick1.wav, snare1.wav, hihat1.wav and piano_c1.wav.

### `fresh_id`

```java
public static String fresh_id(String name)
```

A new element's identifier: `name`, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. Sends nothing; what `command` makes takes it.

### `command`

```java
public static void command(String kind, String id, String text, String numbers, int mode)
```

Sends the page one command, by `kind`, with an element `id`, a `text` and its `numbers` as words. Sound: "play" (id the sample; numbers at volume rate pan channel reverse), "start" (id a new voice, text the sample, numbers as play's then loop), "stop" (at), "fade" (volume over), "stop_all", "tone" (text the wave; frequency at duration volume pan channel), "master" (volume), "tempo" (bpm), "swing" (amount), "beat" (steps; reports "beat" for `id`), "channel" (id the channel; volume pan echo echo_time feedback reverb low_pass), "listen" (bins smoothing), "audio" (text pause or resume), "render" and "render_end". Timers: "after" and "every" (seconds; reports "timer"), "cancel". The page: "set_text", "visible" and "enabled" (1 or 0), "remove", "text_area" (rows columns), "file_button", "cursor", "save_canvas", "download". `mode` says what a page connecting later is sent again: 0 kept, 1 the last of its kind and id, 2 like a sound, 3 nothing.

### `watch`

```java
public static void watch(String id, String kind, Runnable f)
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`: a timer's "timer", a beat's "beat", a text area's "change", a file button's "loaded", a rendering's "rendered".

### `report_number`

```java
public static double report_number(String name, int k)
```

The `k`th number the page last reported under `name`: "clock" (the beat, the latency, whether sound runs), "beat" (a beat's step and time), "level", "band" and "wave" once listening, "rendered" (seconds taken, peak). 0.0 where there is none.

### `report_text`

```java
public static String report_text(String name)
```

The text the page last reported under `name`: "value." and an input's identifier for what it holds, "file" and "file.text" for a file loaded. Empty where there is none.

### `report_count`

```java
public static int report_count(String name)
```

How many numbers the page last reported under `name`.

### `watch_text`

```java
public static void watch_text(String id, String kind, String name, Consumer<String> f)
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`, with the text it last reported under `name`: a text area's "change" with "value." and its identifier, a file button's "loaded" with "file".

### `watch_step`

```java
public static void watch_step(String id, String kind, BiConsumer<Integer, Double> f)
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`, with the first number reported under `kind` as a whole number and the second: a beat's step and when it sounds.

### `watch_pair`

```java
public static void watch_pair(String id, String kind, BiConsumer<Double, Double> f)
```

Calls `f` each time the page reports `kind` for the element `id`, with the first two numbers reported under `kind`: a rendering's seconds taken and its peak.

### `splash`

```java
public static void splash()
```

Shows the splash screen: the page dimmed, and a message asking the reader to click, since a browser plays no sound before the reader has clicked or pressed a key. The page waits there -- what the program draws next, its frames and its clock -- until the reader does. It is shown at most once, and not at all where the reader has already clicked. The first `play_sample` before a click shows it too; a program that plays sound only from callbacks calls it at the end of its main code.

### `set_splash`

```java
public static void set_splash(String message)
```

Sets what the splash screen says, "Click to Start" until it is set. An empty `message` turns the splash screen off.

### `time`

```java
public static double time()
```

The page's clock, in seconds, as the page last reported it: inside an `on_frame` callback, the time the frame is for. It is the audio clock once sound has started, so a time read here is a time `play_sample` can be given.

### `sdelay`

```java
public static void sdelay(double time)
```

Waits until the page's audio clock is `time` seconds after the last `sdelay` ended (after now, for the first), so a loop of them does not drift; one that has fallen behind goes on at once. The page's events are delivered while it waits, and a sound played next with no time of its own starts exactly at the end.

### `on_frame`

```java
public static void on_frame(Consumer<Double> draw)
```

Calls `draw` before each frame the page shows, with the time the frame is for.

### `on_mouse`

```java
public static void on_mouse(String c, BiConsumer<Integer, Integer> click)
```

Calls `click` with the position, in pixels from the top left corner, of every click on the canvas `c`.

### `on_key`

```java
public static void on_key(Consumer<String> pressed)
```

Calls `pressed` with the name of every key pressed while the page has the focus: a letter or digit as itself, and otherwise the browser's name for it, such as "ArrowLeft", "Enter" or " ".

### `on_key_up`

```java
public static void on_key_up(Consumer<String> released)
```

Calls `released` with the name of each key let go while the page has the focus. Leaving the page lets go of every key held.

### `key_down`

```java
public static boolean key_down(String key)
```

Whether the key named `key` is held down now.

### lib_tinyweb_beat

```pyking norun
# tinyweb's beat, listening and rendering: a step sequencer's callback
# told each step and when it sounds, the tempo and swing changed, the
# sound paused and resumed, the level, bands and wave the page reports,
# and a few seconds rendered into a file. The .events file stands in
# for the page.

import tinyweb as tw
import tinyweb.sound as sound

tw.web_init(0)
kick = tw.load_sample("kick1.wav")
hat = tw.load_sample("hihat1.wav")
sound.tempo(120.0)
sound.swing(0.2)
sound.listen(bins = 8, smoothing = 0.5)


def step(n: Int, time: Float):
    print("step", n, "at", time, "beat", sound.beat())
    if n - n / 4 * 4 == 0:
        tw.play(kick, at = time)
    tw.play(hat, at = time, volume = 0.3)
    if n == 2:
        sound.tempo(90.0)


steps = sound.on_beat(step, steps = 2)
print(steps)


def listened():
    print("level", sound.level(), "bands", sound.bands(), sound.band(0), sound.band(7), "wave", sound.wave(0), sound.wave(3))


tw.button("Listen", on_click = listened)


def toggle(on: Bool):
    if on:
        sound.resume()
    else:
        sound.pause()
    print("playing", on)


tw.checkbox("Playing", checked = true, on_change = toggle)


def song():
    tw.play(kick)
    tw.play(kick, at = 0.5)
    sound.tone(220.0, at = 1.0, duration = 0.25)


def done(took: Float, peak: Float):
    print("rendered in", took, "seconds, peak", peak)


sound.render_wav(2.0, song, name = "song.wav", on_rendered = done)
sound.render_wav(1.0, song)
print("latency", sound.latency())
```

tinyweb’s Java implementation is a library of its own: a Java program can use it to draw on a web page, add buttons, labels and sliders to it, play sounds and answer the reader, with no Pyking anywhere. It is the file Pyking copies beside a program compiled for java21, renamed Tinyweb.java.

Download tinyweb-java.zip: Tinyweb.java, the example below, and the samples in tinyweb_assets/.

Running a program

The program serves its own page: web_init starts the server and prints its address, and once the program’s own code has finished it goes on serving the page and calling the functions it handed over until it is stopped (Ctrl-C). Open the address in a browser.

The page asks for a sample beside where the program runs first, then in tinyweb_assets/ there.

An example

Functions

Every function but web_init needs web_init to have been called first, or PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG to be set (below); otherwise it says so and the program ends with status 1.

web_init

Serves the program’s page on port and prints its address, tinyweb: http://127.0.0.1:N/; port 0 picks any free port. Call it before anything else. With PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG set it does nothing.

canvas

A new canvas, width by height pixels, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it: “canvas”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

fill_canvas

Fills the whole canvas c with color, a CSS color such as "#ff0000" or "red".

draw_shape

One shape on the canvas c. kind is “rect”, “circle”, “ellipse”, “arc”, “line”, “lines”, “curve”, “bezier”, “polygon”, “path” or “erase”, and numbers its numbers as words: x y width height radius for a rect, x y r for a circle, x y rx ry for an ellipse, x y r start end (radians) for an arc, x1 y1 x2 y2 for a line, x1 y1 x2 y2 for each of many lines, x1 y1 cx cy x2 y2 for a curve, x1 y1 ax ay bx by x2 y2 for a bezier, x y x y … for a polygon or a path, and x y width height for the rectangle erase makes transparent. It is filled with color and outlined with outline, width pixels thick, each unless it is "", at alpha from 0.0 to 1.0. A color may be a gradient: “linear-gradient(x1 y1 x2 y2); 0.0 red; 1.0 blue”, “radial-gradient(x1 y1 r1 x2 y2 r2); …” or “conic-gradient(x y angle); …”, each stop its place from 0.0 to 1.0 and a CSS color.

draw_pairs

Many shapes’ numbers in one go, as a list rather than as words: kind “polygon” or “path” through the points (x, y) in items, drawn as draw_shape draws one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

draw_triples

Many circles in one go: kind “circles”, each (x, y, radius) in items filled and outlined on its own, as draw_shape draws one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

draw_quads

Many separate lines in one go: kind “lines”, each (x1, y1, x2, y2) in items, stroked together as one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

draw_text

words written on the canvas c at (x, y): its left end there, or with align “center” or “right” its middle or right end, and its top there, or with baseline “middle”, “alphabetic” or “bottom” that part of it. size pixels high, in font ("" for the page’s own), bold where bold is true, filled with color and outlined with outline outline_width pixels thick, each unless it is "", at alpha.

set_state

Changes what the next drawing on the canvas c is drawn with. kind “translate”, “rotate” or “scale” take their numbers (x y, radians, sx sy) in numbers; “push” and “pop” save and restore the state; “reset” takes every transformation off; “shadow” takes a color in value ("" for none) and blur dx dy in numbers; “blend” takes “normal” or “add” in value; “line_style” takes how lines end and turn in value (“round round”, “butt miter”, …) and the dash offset followed by the dash and gap lengths in numbers; “clip” keeps what is drawn after it inside a shape, its kind in value and its numbers as draw_shape takes them. fill_canvas starts the canvas afresh.

measure

Asks the page how wide words is written size pixels high in font, bold where bold is true, and calls answer with the width in pixels once the page has said.

watch_pointer

Calls f with where the pointer is on the canvas c, in pixels from its top left corner, each time it goes down there (kind “press”), comes up (“release”), moves over it (“move”) or moves with the button held (“drag”).

pointer

Where the pointer was last seen on the canvas c: which “x” or “y” for its position, “down” for 1 while its button is held and 0 otherwise. The canvas reports the pointer once watch_pointer has been called for it.

draw_image

Draws a loaded picture on the canvas c, its top left corner at (x, y), stretched to width by height, at alpha. One still loading is drawn once it has loaded, and what is drawn after it waits until then.

make_bitmap

A picture width by height pixels the program builds, every pixel background to start with, as set_pixel takes a color, kept by the program: setting a pixel sends nothing. Answers the string that names it: “bitmap”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

set_pixel

Sets the pixel (x, y) of the bitmap b to color, red times 65536 plus green times 256 plus blue. A pixel outside it is left alone.

get_pixel

The color of the pixel (x, y) of the bitmap b, as set_pixel takes one; 0 outside it.

fill_bitmap

Sets every pixel of the bitmap b to color.

draw_bitmap

Draws the bitmap b on the canvas c, its top left corner at (x, y), each pixel scale pixels across: sharp squares above 1.0. What changed since it was last drawn is sent to the page.

load_image

Starts loading the picture name, looked for as a sample is, and answers the string that names it to draw_image.

make_button

A button showing title, placed below what the page already shows, which calls on_click each time it is pressed. Answers the string that names it: title, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

label

A line of text, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it to set_label: text, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

row

A box placed below what the page already shows, whose elements go side by side, wrapping where the page is too narrow. Answers the string that names it to inside: “row”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

column

A box whose elements go one below another, as the page’s own do: inside a row, it stands beside the row’s other elements. Answers the string that names it to inside.

inside

Makes every element made after it go into the row or column id, until outside or another inside.

outside

Makes every element made after it go on the page again, below what is there.

set_label

Replaces the text of the label id, or the title of the button id, with text.

make_slider

A slider from low to high, starting at value, placed below what the page already shows, which calls on_change with each new value it is moved to. Answers the string that names it: “slider”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

make_checkbox

A checkbox showing title, ticked where checked is true, which calls on_change with whether it is ticked each time the reader changes it. Answers the string that names it.

make_radio

A radio button showing title in the group group: choosing one clears the others. The first of a group starts chosen unless one says chosen. Calls on_pick with title when the reader chooses it. Answers the string that names it.

make_choice

A dropdown of options, one per line, the one at position chosen chosen, which calls on_change with the position the reader chooses. Answers the string that names it.

make_text_input

A line to type text into, showing placeholder while empty, which calls on_enter with the text when Enter is pressed in it. Answers the string that names it.

make_number_input

A field for a whole number from low to high, starting at value, which calls on_change with each new number. Answers the string that names it.

set_checked

Ticks or clears the checkbox id, or chooses the radio button id.

set_value

Moves the slider or number field id to value, or picks the dropdown choice at that position.

apply_style

Changes the page’s look. With kind “theme”, value names a theme: “light” (the default), “dark”, “plain”, “paper” or “retro”. With kind “page”, “button”, “label”, “slider” or “canvas”, property of every element of that kind becomes value; with kind “element”, only the element id’s. property is one of background, color, border, radius, font, size, padding, gap, accent and width, and value is CSS, such as “#336699” or “12px”. id is "" except for an element.

load_sample

Starts loading the sound file name and answers a string naming it to play_sample: name, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. The name is looked up beside where the program runs first, and then among the samples tinyweb ships in tinyweb_assets/: kick1.wav, snare1.wav, hihat1.wav and piano_c1.wav.

fresh_id

A new element’s identifier: name, with a number added where something on the page has that name already. Sends nothing; what command makes takes it.

command

Sends the page one command, by kind, with an element id, a text and its numbers as words. Sound: “play” (id the sample; numbers at volume rate pan channel reverse), “start” (id a new voice, text the sample, numbers as play’s then loop), “stop” (at), “fade” (volume over), “stop_all”, “tone” (text the wave; frequency at duration volume pan channel), “master” (volume), “tempo” (bpm), “swing” (amount), “beat” (steps; reports “beat” for id), “channel” (id the channel; volume pan echo echo_time feedback reverb low_pass), “listen” (bins smoothing), “audio” (text pause or resume), “render” and “render_end”. Timers: “after” and “every” (seconds; reports “timer”), “cancel”. The page: “set_text”, “visible” and “enabled” (1 or 0), “remove”, “text_area” (rows columns), “file_button”, “cursor”, “save_canvas”, “download”. mode says what a page connecting later is sent again: 0 kept, 1 the last of its kind and id, 2 like a sound, 3 nothing.

watch

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id: a timer’s “timer”, a beat’s “beat”, a text area’s “change”, a file button’s “loaded”, a rendering’s “rendered”.

report_number

The kth number the page last reported under name: “clock” (the beat, the latency, whether sound runs), “beat” (a beat’s step and time), “level”, “band” and “wave” once listening, “rendered” (seconds taken, peak). 0.0 where there is none.

report_text

The text the page last reported under name: “value.” and an input’s identifier for what it holds, “file” and “file.text” for a file loaded. Empty where there is none.

report_count

How many numbers the page last reported under name.

watch_text

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id, with the text it last reported under name: a text area’s “change” with “value.” and its identifier, a file button’s “loaded” with “file”.

watch_step

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id, with the first number reported under kind as a whole number and the second: a beat’s step and when it sounds.

watch_pair

Calls f each time the page reports kind for the element id, with the first two numbers reported under kind: a rendering’s seconds taken and its peak.

splash

Shows the splash screen: the page dimmed, and a message asking the reader to click, since a browser plays no sound before the reader has clicked or pressed a key. The first play_sample before a click shows it too; a program that plays sound only from callbacks calls it at the end of its main code.

Sets what the splash screen says, “Click to Start” until it is set. An empty message turns the splash screen off.

time

The page’s clock, in seconds, as the page last reported it: inside an on_frame callback, the time the frame is for. It is the audio clock once sound has started, so a time read here is a time play_sample can be given.

sdelay

Waits until the page’s audio clock is time seconds after the last sdelay ended (after now, for the first), so a loop of them does not drift; one that has fallen behind goes on at once. The page’s events are delivered while it waits, and a sound played next with no time of its own starts exactly at the end.

Calls draw before each frame the page shows, with the time the frame is for.

on_mouse

Calls click with the position, in pixels from the top left corner, of every click on the canvas c.

on_key

Calls pressed with the name of every key pressed while the page has the focus: a letter or digit as itself, and otherwise the browser’s name for it, such as “ArrowLeft”, “Enter” or ” ”.

on_key_up

Calls released with the name of each key let go while the page has the focus. Leaving the page lets go of every key held.

key_down

Whether the key named key is held down now.

An example

Every function but web_init needs web_init to have been called first, or PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG to be set (below); otherwise it says so and the program ends with status 1.

web_init

Serves the program’s page on port and prints its address, tinyweb: http://127.0.0.1:N/; port 0 picks any free port. Call it before anything else. With PYKING_TINYWEB_LOG set it does nothing.

canvas

A new canvas, width by height pixels, placed below what the page already shows. Answers the string that names it: “canvas”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

fill_canvas

Fills the whole canvas c with color, a CSS color such as "#ff0000" or "red".

draw_shape

One shape on the canvas c. kind is “rect”, “circle”, “ellipse”, “arc”, “line”, “lines”, “curve”, “bezier”, “polygon”, “path” or “erase”, and numbers its numbers as words: x y width height radius for a rect, x y r for a circle, x y rx ry for an ellipse, x y r start end (radians) for an arc, x1 y1 x2 y2 for a line, x1 y1 x2 y2 for each of many lines, x1 y1 cx cy x2 y2 for a curve, x1 y1 ax ay bx by x2 y2 for a bezier, x y x y … for a polygon or a path, and x y width height for the rectangle erase makes transparent. It is filled with color and outlined with outline, width pixels thick, each unless it is "", at alpha from 0.0 to 1.0. A color may be a gradient: “linear-gradient(x1 y1 x2 y2); 0.0 red; 1.0 blue”, “radial-gradient(x1 y1 r1 x2 y2 r2); …” or “conic-gradient(x y angle); …”, each stop its place from 0.0 to 1.0 and a CSS color.

draw_pairs

Many shapes’ numbers in one go, as a list rather than as words: kind “polygon” or “path” through the points (x, y) in items, drawn as draw_shape draws one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

draw_triples

Many circles in one go: kind “circles”, each (x, y, radius) in items filled and outlined on its own, as draw_shape draws one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

draw_quads

Many separate lines in one go: kind “lines”, each (x1, y1, x2, y2) in items, stroked together as one. Not in C, which cannot be given a list.

draw_text

words written on the canvas c at (x, y): its left end there, or with align “center” or “right” its middle or right end, and its top there, or with baseline “middle”, “alphabetic” or “bottom” that part of it. size pixels high, in font ("" for the page’s own), bold where bold is true, filled with color and outlined with outline outline_width pixels thick, each unless it is "", at alpha.

set_state

Changes what the next drawing on the canvas c is drawn with. kind “translate”, “rotate” or “scale” take their numbers (x y, radians, sx sy) in numbers; “push” and “pop” save and restore the state; “reset” takes every transformation off; “shadow” takes a color in value ("" for none) and blur dx dy in numbers; “blend” takes “normal” or “add” in value; “line_style” takes how lines end and turn in value (“round round”, “butt miter”, …) and the dash offset followed by the dash and gap lengths in numbers; “clip” keeps what is drawn after it inside a shape, its kind in value and its numbers as draw_shape takes them. fill_canvas starts the canvas afresh.

Asks the page how wide words is written size pixels high in font, bold where bold is true, and calls answer with the width in pixels once the page has said.

watch_pointer

Calls f with where the pointer is on the canvas c, in pixels from its top left corner, each time it goes down there (kind “press”), comes up (“release”), moves over it (“move”) or moves with the button held (“drag”).

Where the pointer was last seen on the canvas c: which “x” or “y” for its position, “down” for 1 while its button is held and 0 otherwise. The canvas reports the pointer once watch_pointer has been called for it.

make_bitmap

A picture width by height pixels the program builds, every pixel background to start with, as set_pixel takes a color, kept by the program: setting a pixel sends nothing. Answers the string that names it: “bitmap”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

Sets the pixel (x, y) of the bitmap b to color, red times 65536 plus green times 256 plus blue. A pixel outside it is left alone.

make_button

A button showing title, placed below what the page already shows, which calls on_click each time it is pressed. Answers the string that names it: title, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

label

row

A box placed below what the page already shows, whose elements go side by side, wrapping where the page is too narrow. Answers the string that names it to inside: “row”, with a number added where something on the page has that name already.

column

A box whose elements go one below another, as the page’s own do: inside a row, it stands beside the row’s other elements. Answers the string that names it to inside.

Replaces the text of the label id, or the title of the button id, with text.
